message.content: {"caption":"Three-panel grouped bar chart comparing success rates across model transfers and programming-task domains.","description":"A three-panel grouped bar chart with percentage success rate on each vertical axis. The shared legend identifies Initial Agent (gray), Best Agent transfer to other FMs (pale blue), Best Agent from DGM (blue), Aider (green), DGM search on all language (purple), and DGM search only on python (orange). All bars have printed percentage labels; there are no arrows or other marks. Left panel, “Model Transfer on SWE-bench,” has an axis from 0% to 60% and compares o3-mini, Claude 3.5 Sonnet (New), and Claude 3.7 Sonnet: initial-agent scores are 23.0%, 20.0%, and 19.0%; the corresponding other bars are 33.0% for transfer to other FMs, 50.0% for the best agent from DGM, and 59.0% for transfer to other FMs. Middle panel, “Model Transfer on Polyglot,” has an axis from 0% to 40% and the same model categories: initial-agent scores are 14.2%, 32.0%, and 35.6%; the corresponding DGM or transfer scores are 30.7%, 33.3%, and 36.8%. Thus the DGM/transfer bar exceeds the initial-agent bar in each model comparison, with the largest gaps for o3-mini. Right panel, “Task Transfer on Polyglot,” has an axis from 0% to 40% and compares python task with non-python task. For python tasks, initial agent is 8.8%, Aider 11.8%, DGM search on all language 17.6%, and DGM search only on python 20.6%. For non-python tasks, the respective scores are 15.2%, 17.3%, 33.0%, and 30.8%. DGM search only on python is highest for python tasks, while DGM search on all language is highest for non-python tasks; every method scores higher on non-python than python tasks in this
